speaker: The Chairman
text: Head I, Ministry of Social and Family Development.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is clear from the outpouring of support during COVID-19 that many Singaporeans want to do their part and help each other.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This can be done in formal networks – through Government funding, schemes and institutions, but also, and perhaps more powerfully, through collaboration with informal networks – neighbours, friends and communities, including online communities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Over the years, the formal networks have taken more care, and certainly less bureaucratic, less bloodless approach to help families in a holistic manner.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In addition, the old governance philosophy of red tape and jumping through hoops has been replaced by a more respectful calibration, and thicker network of attention and care.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Today, we have one stop centres, we have multiple agencies working together, we have a lens focused on the person, and not a collection of problems.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Second, what has been the main gap that the SSOs have identified?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Is there anything else that is missing in our delivery system?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Have we asked for feedback from the families and people that we have helped, and see what we can do to improve the services?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Last, but not least, how can we better harness the power of the community to strengthen support for those in need?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: How can we seed and how can we facilitate such community efforts to maximise the impact and benefits to Singaporeans?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, if you would like to take your next two cuts together, please do.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As social needs grow, it is important for the Government and the community to partner each other to better meet these needs.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I had earlier spoken on the power of community in terms of delivery of social services.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We can harness the same power in partnership.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Even as we take care in terms of fiscal prudence, audits and careful use of public monies, we must also count in the intangibles that such networks bring.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How does the Ministry intend to strengthen such partnerships?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: What are some of the safeguards and audit measures we can bring into play No one likes an overweening state – and help comes much faster, and in much a friendlier form, when organised and implemented by people we know.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We need strong partners in the community and it is useful to see how much the people and public sector can work together.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Singapore's social safety net was the first and strongest weapon we had against the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This net – which allowed us some measure of certainty in a very precarious situation, comprised financial assistance, as well as social support such as employment assistance and jobs creation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is thanks to this that we dodged many of the bullets that we now see, even in developed countries – the long queues of people at food banks, the homeless on the streets, the disproportionately larger load of poorer people in hospital due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It may seem here that COVID-19 hurt the poor and the rich equally hard, at least in terms of vulnerability to the virus.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: However, we must open our eyes to the fact that in any downturn, any downturn, it is the poorest among us who are the most vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Ministry also provide an update on job creation efforts in the social sector?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We need all of us to emerge stronger from the pandemic – not just the strongest, but the weakest among us too.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I think we did right in focusing the bulk of our help to help businesses preserve jobs, but I think we must also work at the social end of the stick – take stock of how well the measures worked, what more we need to do, and what we need to change.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Let us focus on the outcomes, I would like an update on that.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Chairman, since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, this Government has moved quickly and decisively to strengthen our social safety net to support Singaporeans who have lost their livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The expansion in our financial assistance schemes, as well as the strengthening of our social support systems, in areas such as employment assistance and jobs creation, have been helpful in assisting the vulnerable segments of our society.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Care-givers are an important pillar of our social safety net, performing their duties invisibly, to prevent vulnerable Singaporeans from falling onto the Government's social safety net.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We need to provide better support to the invisible hands that help us to stich the safety nets above the state's current resources.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Is there a need to increase the number of jobs in this vital sector, so that we leave no vulnerable Singaporean behind?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has brought to the fore the important role of our social service delivery.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In order for our social service delivery to reach the needy, we must increase public awareness and boost our detection mechanism.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Awareness is the beginning of the delivery process.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Awareness of where and how to get help will draw those who need it.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the other hand, there are people who need help but do not or are unable to seek assistance for various reasons.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If the SSOs or the communities are aware of them, we will be able to reach out to them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, many disadvantaged families and individuals have a range of needs which require intervention by different community agencies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, not all their needs are always presented to the officers and volunteers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How will the SSOs and SSAs improve on their abilities to detect such issues to ensure that their cases receive holistic help?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: When encountered with complex cases, how do the various teams of professional staff and volunteers coordinate their work?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What procedures are in place to minimize duplications and blind spots?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another point I wish to make is making it easier for the applicants to access help.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, I would like to suggest that we locate mini-SSOs in areas where rental blocks are sited as most of the residents who need help reside in our HDB rental blocks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The mini-SSOs can pull in the necessary resources from the neighbourhood or nearby precincts to help the varied needs of these vulnerable families and provide them with holistic assistance.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Help can be more targeted as they cater to these few rental blocks in this particular precinct.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, Sir, during the COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore, we witness many acts of kindness especially the lost, the least and the last in society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I work with some of the best social service professionals from MSF and social service agencies, grassroots and non-grassroots volunteers in my district.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Despite this, there are still gaps in the last mile of social service delivery that need to be addressed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I will touch on three Cs – Coordination, communication and ComLink.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A common sight on the ground especially in rental housing estates is an overlap of services such as free distribution of food, masks, groceries, health screening and even home cleaning.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: During a recent long weekend before the Lunar New Year, I met six groups, some are regular and some are ad hoc, distributing lunch bento boxes to the same group of rental residents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there a more effective way of coordination so that there is less overlap, less wastage and better allocation of precious resources?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Yet, from my work with many Social Service partners, including volunteer groups, such as Mummy Yummy, Homeless HEARTS and Keeping Hope Alive, I know that many current help channels do exist.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Ministry facilitate a national communication plan at both strategic and tactical level, so that many more know where to get help or to help signpost where help can be obtained?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My CDC, of course, would be a willing partner.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In Central District which I oversee, there are many elderly singles and couples living in rental flats.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can ComLink be scaled to include these households although the elderly, for example, are technically under MOH.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can Government give more resources to MSF so that can comb entire rental housing blocks and not only specific profiles?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I would like to urge the Government to consider implementing a seamless application process for the disadvantaged children who require financial assistance to attend schools.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Social Service Offices’ records about their families can be shared with MOE and schools, so that the children do not need to apply for the Financial Assistance Scheme, school pocket money fund and other related programmes separately.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For the underprivileged families, the adults are already struggling with a multitude of problems.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Navigating assistance schemes is not easy for them, much less for their children.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As a Smart Nation, we can tap upon information technology to make the process easier for all stakeholders using data integration.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The seamless integrated financial assistance application process will need more proactive and closer collaboration amongst the involved Ministries – MSF, MOH’s NEHR MND as well as the approved financial service centre's database on kids studying or staying in the rental HDB units.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: These clusters were selected due to the sizeable number of families and children living in rental flats in those areas.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Minister Desmond Lee mentioned in Parliament that, "Most importantly, ComLink will develop a sense of community and mutual help, with neighbours supporting one another in their journeys." Since its inception, has the pilot succeeded in meeting its intended outcomes?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Moreover, are there any learning points to be taken away from this pilot project?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Also, are there any plans to extend this programme to leverage local community partnerships to support the needs of the families?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: If so, how will this programme be scalable on a national level in the coming future?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, I just realised it is quite apt that the mask I am wearing today has a 招财猫 on it because my next cut is about money and donations.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, while donations for specific causes such as supporting those affected by the pandemic have increased, many other organisations have experienced a reduction in donations due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This could hamper the ability to deliver essential social services on the ground and Deputy Prime Minister Heng himself has noted that, and I quote, "Some charities even had to dip into their reserves to keep operations going.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This affects the help that goes to those who need it." As such, what are the Ministry's plans to encourage more giving despite this on-going challenging times?

speaker: The Chairman
text: If you would like to take both your cuts together, please do.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This could not be more timely as we know many charities, VWOs and social service agencies are currently facing a challenging environment caused by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We should certainly encourage individuals to give as part of their daily lives; ComChest should also partner and make it convenient for businesses to provide opportunities for customers to donate through their payment platforms.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We all know that Singaporeans, everyone here, has a big heart.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, if we make that facility available, convenient and accessible, I think great things could come out of it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Now putting on my hat as the group CEO of NTUC Fairprice, I want to assure Minister that we will certainly give this scheme a full consideration and do our part to make lives better for the community.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We often think little children spend most of their school time in physical activity and play – which many do – and rightly so.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: However, the experience of the pandemic has taught us that there will be occasions when pre-school students will have to stay at home for long periods as well.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: How will the pre-school sector be supported to emerge stronger from the experience of COVID-19?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Pre-school teachers may benefit from more training, which will enable them to explore innovations in online teaching methods.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They could also be supported with grants and new hardware as well as software, so as to allow them to contribute to their students’ development, even when teaching from home.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Second, can we also explore how pre-schools administration can benefit from greater digitalisation, including providing their staff with remote working and learning opportunities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Our pre-school teachers are some of the most imaginative and dedicated in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have quite a few of them in our NTUC First Campus.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We must help them to succeed in a digital world.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am not saying to lower the budget for it, but I am saying we need a clear strategy to supplement ComCare, aimed at empowering families beyond surviving, to facilitate their thriving and reduce their recidivism back to financial support.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And to do this, we need more people who are well-versed in discovering and harnessing the assets and strengths of the community, and to transform the current recipients of aid into active contributors in the community and also pave their way towards higher employability.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this because I see a ripe opportunity for the transformation of our social services sector.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: An opportunity to develop empathy and empowerment at scale, to better harness the strengths within our challenged individuals and families.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: While I am grateful for the numerous COVID-19 support schemes that have been given out so far, frontline administrators in our SSOs are over-stretched and inundated with very onerous but necessary task of administrative checks and gatekeeping.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And we need to help them out, and we can, by augmenting the sector with more personnel, trained professionally in asset-based community development.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: With many professionals impacted by lay-offs and a surge in community spirit brought by COVID-19, we now have a pool of highly qualified people, who are seeking more meaningful careers that can be harnessed for the social services sector.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MSF can accelerate its support to the sector and enhance ComLink’s efforts by appointing qualified Social Service Agencies with good track records to train mid-career entrants in community-building and assets discovery work.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Trained personnel can then be hired and deployed through SSOs or grassroots organisations.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This will help SSOs to enhance its function beyond administrators of support schemes and connectors within the community to become effective community builders.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: With that, I would like to convey my high hopes for ComLink, and I look forward to more job creation in the social services sector, to enable the empowerment of our ComCare recipients into a community that thrives.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, may I take my cuts together?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Together with your cut at (o), you mean?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: The community, including the social service agencies (SSAs), community groups and corporates, play a critical role alongside the Government in supporting the social needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Amidst the disruption caused by COVID-19, we saw many SSAs that rose to the occasion and adapted to the new operating environment to deliver social services to those in need.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: However, it was also through this crisis that we have learnt that we will need to have better coordination amongst different SSAs to leverage on one another’s strengthen and expertise to deliver targeted assistance to families to better identify specific needs with the most appropriate solution at the right time.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: We have also learnt that we need to further strengthen our outreach capabilities and ability to communicate with those in need, especially remotely via teleconferencing.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Many SSAs can reap productivity gains if they have had deployed suitable toolkits and platforms within their organisations.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: However, many lack the resources and the capacity to develop and maintain these capabilities.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: COVID-19 is one of the first major crisis in the lives of many youths.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Due to the disruption in routines and social activities, many youth’s mental health and well-being were affected.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Education, awareness and timely persistent community support are important aspects to ensure that our youths develop resilience, understanding and pathways to better manage their own mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Friends, family, loved ones and those around, must have a keen ability to identify symptoms.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In other cases, a better understanding of the youths' environment can help identity risk factors and mitigating measure early.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Can MSF update on how the youth mental well-being network can help support our youths' mental health and well-being through future crisis and COVID-19 and beyond?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This increase by just two years would require real adjustments by the various agencies involved to cater to the older youths between 16 and 18 years of age.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Another significant change is the new FGO regime which provides for compulsory attendance at family programmes even before parents can file a court application.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The amendments were effective in July 2020 and I appreciate that only half a year has passed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, what is MSF's interim assessment of the impact?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For instance, how have the juvenile rehabilitation centres cope with increase and different caseload?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Have children been better served under the FGO regime compared to the BPC regime?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, youths continue to feature significantly in the crime trends involving drug abuse, secret societies and criminal activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Recently, there was also a disturbing report of a youth being self-radicalised to become a terrorist.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How do we help such youths through their families and other partners such as schools, self-help groups and social service agencies to build up their resilience to guard against such negative influences, ensure that each of them will be given opportunities to realise their full potential?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What has been the outcome of the measures put in place to assist youths at risk thus far?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These are the focus areas of my speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It was to have lasted three years, with the aim of helping 900 young people through 10 service providers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These agencies would then be trained and use standardised assessment tools to their work with young people.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In 2018, the Government set up the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recividism (NCPR) to oversee national efforts to prevent offending, re-offending and enhance rehabilitation of offenders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The scope of NCPR includes at risk children and youth.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Working with people whether young or old, requires a human-centred approach, being sensitive to specific home contexts as well as the personality of the youth.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mentorship was a topic that the hon Member of Parliament Miss Rachel Ong touched on during the Budget debate last week when she proposed that youths at risk have long-term mentors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It will be good to understand what has been the outcome of these programmes to date?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Relatedly, do we have enough youth workers, and do they receive enough support?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What emerging threats does the Minister see among our young people today that we need to guard against?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, our youth today are woke about mental health and well-being, not only for themselves but also in terms of how all of us as a society have a role to play to support and journey with those who are coping with mental health challenges.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Our youths are woke about acting on mental health, acting on the reservoir of stigma that still persists today and woke about encouraging and making sure that all those who need help actually come forward to seek help.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: How can the Ministry better support our youths in their efforts to advance and champion mental well-being and, specifically, the Ministry has set up a Youth Mental Well-being Network?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can I ask what is the role of this Network, what has been its progress, especially in terms of outcomes and what are the Ministry's future plans for the Network?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Moreover, youth participation in social groups has generally gone up from ages between 15 and 34 years old from 2010 to 2016.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Besides the increase in youth volunteerism and participation rates, our youth have also made remarkable contribution to our community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: In 2018, then Minister for Culture, Community and Youth, Minister Grace Fu, underscored the story of Kenneth and Yin Loong who were among the 15 youth who received Meritorious Youth Award at the People's Association Youth Movement Awards and Central Youth Council Installation ceremonies.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Both Yin Loong and Kenneth have been volunteering for more than a decade.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Through the Day of Giving series, Yin Loong in Kolam Ayer CCYEC organised food ration contributions and movie screenings for the disadvantaged.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: In 2017, Day of Giving mobilised 200 student volunteers to make 8,000 cupcakes for old folks' homes island-wide.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Therefore, besides the increased rates of youth volunteerism and community involvement, our youth have made deep and everlasting impact on our social fabric.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: In light of heartening trend of youth volunteerism and community development, how have we empowered and supported our youth to build a more resilient and inclusive society together?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As such, while there may be vacancies in the system today, this may not be so for particular areas with high concentration of young families.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Chairman, the efficiency of our nation is powered by many hardworking men and women who work around the clock to support us – the workers who start packing your online orders in the warehouses at midnight, the healthcare staff who tend to our sick and wounded as our city sleeps, the fishmongers who collect our seafood supplies from Jurong Fishery Port, the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: For shift workers who do not have family support and cannot afford to hire a foreign domestic helper, getting evening and overnight childcare services for their young children is a big challenge.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: There have been cases where lower Primary school kids are tasked to look after younger siblings or where children are entrusted to incompetent babysitters.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Chairman, as the early years of people’s lives have such a big impact on their lifelong health, cognitive and psychological conditions, great care should be taken to nurture and develop our children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The Government has committed significant amounts of resources to improve the accessibility, affordability and quality of all our pre-schools.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: However, a child’s development is also heavily dependent on the home environment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: For disadvantaged children, the Government has implemented various initiatives to support their families and enable them to give their children a good start in life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: With holistic assistance measures and more conducive home surroundings, these children will stand a better chance in our competitive economic and social environment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I am heartened that under the KidSTART programme, the development of children from vulnerable families will be monitored and nurtured from the day they were born.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), which leads this programme, provides support for child development and coordinate the social services for the needy families.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How many more regions will KidSTART expand to and how many more children are expected to be covered?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Will the Ministry also provide an update on the status of the "Growing Together with KidSTART" initiative?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: What has been the feedback from the beneficiaries so far?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: ECDA partners the Social Service Offices, Family Service Centres and hospitals to support this group of underprivileged children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Will ECDA consider partnerships with suitable community organisations in the proximity of the children’s homes and with the private sector to widen the scope of programmes which can benefit not just the children but also their families?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling, if you would like to take both your cuts together, please do.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman the importance of early childhood care and education through pre-school cannot be over emphasised in a country like Singapore, where the quality of our human resource has significant impact on our national success.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is still a small fraction of what Singapore normally spends on education system.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad that the shortage of pre-schools in Singapore has been acknowledged and expansion efforts been put in by the Government as early as 2012.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During both the 2017 and 2019 National Day Rallies, Prime Minister Lee also spoke about the initiatives to further develop and boost the pre-school sector.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This may leave parents, whose children are attending the other 50% of pre-schools, wondering about the quality of education that their young children are receiving.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In a few housing estates with high childcare demand, parents are still experiencing waiting times that can range from a few weeks to a few months.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For parents needing to return to work and having no alternative help, this can be a daunting wait.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my constituency, where there are new Build-To-Order (BTO) flats, such as in the Buangkok Crescent area, I regularly receive requests from young couples seeking help to ensure that they can secure a pre-school place for their children in order for both parents to return to work.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I constantly assure them that a place will be availed to them as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Its purpose was to influence peoples' decision to have children in a rapidly ageing society and tackle the nation's long-term demographic change.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To battle Singapore's stubbornly low total fertility rate, we must do more to give assurance to couples that they will not have to worry about having a pre-school place when they give birth to more children.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to accelerate the pace of the roll-out in regions with a higher proportion of younger families.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Knowing that a reliable pre-school can be counted upon to look after their children will be paramount for many young couples to have the confidence to have more children.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Every child is precious, notwithstanding what background they come from or what abilities they have.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Appropriate early-years intervention and support have proven in many research studies to be critical for children with developmental needs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Children with developmental needs deserve a good start in life, the same as any children in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I will always remember fondly of the times that I visited the various Early Intervention Programmes for Infants and Children, or EIPIC, run by the social service agencies during my days in the National Council of Social Service.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Despite their different abilities, seeing these children being given the opportunities to learn and acquire new knowledge and skills was heartening.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I have always hoped for the day when all our pre-schools will be fully inclusive so that our children, with or without disabilities, can learn and grow together.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will not only assimilate children with disabilities or developmental needs to other children of typical growth earlier in their growing years, it can also develop awareness and empathy in children with normal growth to include their peers with different abilities in play and in activities.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Research studies also indicate that typically developing children in inclusive settings perform comparably with or better academically than those in non-inclusive programmes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Mr Chairman, for lower income families, coping with children with special needs is particularly difficult.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: These families are already struggling financially and with children who require more care, their ability to work and earn income is further reduced.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: In addition, therapies and intervention cost money and exert more stress on the families.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: I urge the Government to expedite and increase financial care assistance for them so that they can seek the appropriate therapies for these kids.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: For many cases, regular intervention at the earliest opportunity can make a significant difference to their lives because young minds and bodies are pliable and have great potential to receive and retain treatments.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: With children, we have a "golden period" to help them reduce the severity of their conditions, so we should help the families seize the opportunity without hesitation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: The funds spent on the therapies will be well-invested, subject to the guidance of the Government, who must draw up a list of qualified practitioners.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, in the Parliament Adjournment Motion I filed in October 2020, I called for society to change the way it views persons with disabilities, or PWDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I called for several key gaps to be addressed, for more progress reporting and for more inclusion of the voice of PWDs in policy-making.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wish to speak on two other topics today.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Singapore Government has supported the development of three five-year Enabling Masterplans for the Disabled.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These plans list recommendations to enable PWDs to realise their potential and to become integral and contributing members of society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, I would also like to propose suggestions for the next Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The current Enabling Masterplans take a life-cycle approach and cover general disability issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But the needs of different disability groups are not homogeneous.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I hence propose that the next masterplan also incorporate the inputs of each major disability group.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The autism group, for example, where I help and volunteer, has just completed their own enabling masterplan, which I hope will be supported by the Government and the rest of society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: By encouraging each major disability group to take ownership, study the landscape, prioritise their top needs and invite solutions and partners, the national Enabling Masterplan will be all the more relevant and richer in content.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Masterplans that are five years long also should be constantly updated and reported to reflect the latest achievements and challenges.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The last published third Enabling Masterplan (EMP3), for instance, was not updated with the most significant change of our time—the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, on strengthening disability social service agencies, or SSAs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of the early intervention, special education and services for PWDs are run by these social service agencies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They provide disability expertise and harness the support of the community assets.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Beyond programme grants, the Government has been supportive through measures such as the Government matching of charity donations through the 250% tax exempt benefit and the latest Change for Charity initiative.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I call for the Government to provide more tailored support to its partner SSAs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Smaller SSAs will need greater support in resources such as shared services in fundraising, human resource, volunteer management and financial reporting and compliance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a fallacy that larger charities do not need help nor that they will naturally do well on their own.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Just as Deputy Prime Minister Heng has encouraged the support of large local enterprises (LLEs), so should the same be considered for these larger SSAs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some specific ways of support include the following.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Identify their needs and support larger SSAs as they scale or develop deeper capabilities to move into new essential territories.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Seed and better support the social enterprises of these SSAs so they can help meet targeted social bottom lines that are important for the community such as jobs in sheltered or supported worksites.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, pay or co-fund corporate services such as the CEO and key financial, technology and human resource positions so that these SSAs can focus on and excel in their core services.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Most donors do not fund important corporate services, but these are essential for compliance, for growth and for governance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Help the larger SSAs safely generate better returns from their reserves, which are sometimes large because of the need to save to pay for recurring high-cost services such as day activity centres.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Consider setting aside a percentage of Singapore Savings Bonds or infrastructure bonds for the larger SSAs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The disability sector needs as much help as it can get.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, I gave birth to my son, Ayden, in 2017 and having him is one of the best things that has happened in my life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are some challenges for the family but I have so many things to be grateful for and I am glad for the support that I receive to raise my child.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am grateful for a Government that cares.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is an on-going effort and we need to continue building on existing initiatives, but I am grateful for the effort of the team at MSF, who continues to look at various ways to support PWDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am also grateful for activists and advocates who have blazed a trail for many PWDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Take hon Member, Ms Denise Phua, for example.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Her years of advocacy and labour of love opened the doors for discussions and reviews and led to many meaningful initiatives that have made an impact to the sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would also like to mention Dr Lim Hong Huay and the team at Caring SG.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would declare at this juncture that I have been asked to sit as an advisor to this organisation, but I must sincerely say that I am heartened by the efforts and their passion to support care-givers of PWDs and provide them with helpful resources.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am also truly grateful and indebted to family members and friends who have provided unconditional support and love and have made this journey so much more meaningful.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Their kindness and graciousness have let me to believe that there are many out there who are open and willing, and are keen to see a more inclusive society, one that embraces different abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In my own experience and through conversations with parents of PWDs and people in the disability sector, there are still concerns about the level of understanding and inclusiveness in our society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many parents have shared about unkind remarks people have made to them or the rude stares they receive when their child misbehaves in public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Above all, what families of PWDs hope to see is for their family member to be treated with dignity.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They are no lesser human beings and are as entitled to be treated with respect, like any of us here.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At this juncture, I would like to offer some observations and thoughts on creating a kinder and more inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am heartened by efforts by various agencies like the "See The True Me" campaign and I am always excited to participate in events like the Purple Parade.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe there is now more awareness and sensitivity, but there is still some way to go before we can say that our community is truly inclusive and embracing of people with different abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Do we have indicators in place to help us measure how we are doing as a community and targets which we can work towards?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What more can we do to nudge behaviours and encourage people to be more open and compassionate towards PWDs and their care-givers?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: May be useful to do a review of study so that we could assess a better approach to build on the current efforts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We should equip PWDs with skills and empower the community so that PWDs may contribute to society in some way.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I had in my speech for MOE's COS debate, shared my thoughts on how this could be done in the school setting.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would encourage a similar approach for the workplace and in the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, I think there is a need to engage extensively and meaningfully with employers to create better understanding of different abilities and provide support for the redesigning of jobs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that there are already efforts on this front and it is a challenging exercise.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I feel though, in the long run, there is much value to be gained.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Another area, I believe we could work on, is to develop various infrastructure within our communities to accommodate different needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We do see a few inclusive playgrounds, Braille in the lifts, quiet rooms in public places.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, such awareness and sensitivity to various needs should be more pervasive as we continue to build our common spaces in this country.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, I think we need to continue to educate the community on the appropriate norms or social interactions and empower them to embrace people with different abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We should create opportunities for PWDs to fully participate, physically and socially, in the community, but I think we also need to learn how to do so meaningfully.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have been to events where PWDs were invited to attend as guests, but they were seated at a separate table or space and there was no interaction with the rest of the participants or guests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some families of PWDs would get upset or offended with reactions from the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope that we will continue to grow as a nation, to be one that truly cares for the vulnerable and embrace differences.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Chairman, it may be difficult for some people to understand just exactly how it feels for some of us, to look around this gallery and see so many women in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And it is not just a matter of time, I have done the research.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Even in leading organisations, more can be done to push the envelope, for example ensuring that more women are in leadership positions in revenue functions, in addition to non-revenue, as well as technology functions.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, would you like to take your both cuts together?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This is the year we have set aside to celebrate women.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This may seem, to some of us, to be an artificial effort.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Why do we need a year to celebrate women, when they should be celebrated all the time?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Or, the word "celebration" – is it not condescending to "celebrate" women, as if it is something conferred by the power of men or by institutions?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Added to these are new ones of income and inherited wealth.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Unconscious bias is real, and sometimes, without intending, we do great harm.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In these conversations, and to make any sort of progress, it is important to have some moral clarity.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: One such issue has to do with apologies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Indeed, it is the very nature of unconscious bias that it is unintentional.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, when we apologise, we should certainly make the intentions behind our acts known, but we should also recognise that this is the start and not the end of the matter.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They are mothers, care-givers, workers, and members of our society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And I am encouraged that the Conversations on SG Women's Development is focused on addressing the issues that women face at home, in schools, workplaces and the community in real life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What are some of the issues which have been frequently raised by Singaporeans in the SG Conversation?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In this effort, we must ensure that the interests of all women are represented.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What is the profile in the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In addition, this conversation takes place within a society, a society of all of us.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I recall when I served on the Board of Directors of Centre for Fathering for some 14 years, we had a number of women on our Board – yes on Centre for Fathering.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And the views and insights from these women Board members strengthened the Board and made the organisation better.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Actually this year, it is Centre for Fathering's 20th anniversary.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Speaking of Boards, wearing my NTUC Enterprise hat, in preparing for this cut, I also asked for some statistics on the women representation on our Board.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But there is still progress to be made.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What are some of the practical ways to ensure that women enjoy the same financial freedom as men?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Given that family is the first line of care and support for many Singaporeans, we have traditionally supported and encouraged strong families.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The implicit, normative bias is this – our old mindset that "preservation of families" is inherently good.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The MSF handbook for example, states that, "The guide introduces readers to Intensive Family Preservation in the Singapore context.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This guide offers good practices and intervention strategies.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Readers will uncover knowledge and skills to preserve families and protect children and young persons".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The protection of young children is key and unequivocal.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But I wonder if we need the moral overtones of "intensive preservation".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Can we be more neutral between preservation and creation?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Can we, make a start at least, in according equal respect to the choice between staying in a marriage and leaving it?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In saying this, I do not mean to undermine our commitment to strong families.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Rather, I would like to say that strong families can take different forms.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Some strong families lie within marriages, others are not.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And we ought to make provisions for both.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In so doing, I would like to ask, what is MSF doing to help strengthen familial and couple relations?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In cases where it is not possible to save the marriage, how can we mitigate the negative impact of divorce on children?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In cases where risk factors for divorce are observed earlier, how can we provide better support earlier?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Last, given what I have said about the need for neutrality in choices, but also respecting the need for strong families, how can we together forge a strong narrative in line with the larger Singapore identity?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, our children are often the ones who suffer the most disproportionate consequences in cases of divorce, particularly when the divorce is a high-conflict one and the parents involved are unable to co-parent effectively.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They were less likely to get married themselves, and among those who did, they were more likely to get divorced.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I worry that the added stress and anxiety from the prolonged pandemic might could cause a further deterioration of relations in unstable marriages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lastly, in unfortunate cases where it is not possible to save the marriage, what is the Ministry's plans to mitigate the divorce penalties on our children?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Mr Chairman, I am the final speaker, but I am speaking on a different kind of ending – ending domestic violence.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Domestic violence, particularly those committed against young children, the elderly and people with mental and physical disabilities must be eradicated.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Economic hardships are a trigger for more abuse in a relationship.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: During this pandemic, many survivors of domestic violence feel that they can no longer seek refuge at the home of a friend or relative, for fear they could expose them to the virus.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can we encourage an environment of support whereby neighbours, family members and schools, help to look out for the vulnerable group in our society?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have also to ensure that our Social Service Agency (SSAs) remain financially strong.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They may be under pressure from increased demand and reduced number of volunteers coming forward to help.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As we track the secondary effects of this pandemic, we must consider the impact on family violence and prioritise services.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would the taskforce also be looking beyond family violence, but also domestic violence in general which would include intimate partner violence and violence against other vulnerable groups like foreign domestic workers and the elderly?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts and also partnering MSF through the years, in building a resilient and caring society together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: COVID-19 has plunged societies around the world into one of the most urgent social crises in modern times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For some time, fissures were already bubbling across many societies – exacerbated by new technologies, demography changes and consequent shifts in central gravities from traditional economic powers to newer ones.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many who already left, felt left behind, lost trust in their social systems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must never allow such divisions to take root in our society, especially amid a crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is tough times like these that will test the strength of societies, and the bonds that bind people together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Around the world, how quickly governments and their people worked together, determined whether they could get a reprieve or were overwhelmed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There was a time when Singapore faced a similar crisis as a nation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We had to find practical solutions to our problems of growth and development in our own context, as Mr Lee Kuan Yew said in 1960, even before our independence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our pioneers knew that in order for Singapore to succeed, we needed the tightest economic and social discipline.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With the scarce resources that we had, our priority was to develop a competitive economy, build up a sizeable defence force, and provide basic education, housing and healthcare to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Social assistance at the time was very basic.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Everyone was very much taking care of each other, taking care of themselves and taking care of each other in the family.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We relied on our strong work ethic and that drove economic growth for Singapore – creating employment for the masses.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Leading to improvements in living standards for everyone.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This approach has largely served us well for the first fifty years of our independence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We uplifted an entire population and in one generation rocketed from third world to first.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have also kept public healthcare costs affordable, especially for the lower and middle income groups.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A quality and comprehensive healthcare has enabled our workforce to be up on their feet much of their lives and enjoy their downtime on holidays and not in hospitals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even among the advanced economies, we are one of the few where those at the bottom and in the middle have seen large increases of incomes in the past 20 years, even after accounting for rises in the cost of living.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This means that families have more resources today than before.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We achieved these outcomes without having to go down the paths of other advanced countries, which had to heavily tax their populations to finance their burgeoning social systems, with one generation passing on their debts to the next.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In Singapore, we keep our taxes low for a substantial majority of our population.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want workers to take home as much of what they earned, while at the same time achieving effective transfers for social equity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want to pass down an effective, healthy and debt-free social system, which we have enjoyed and owe this to our children, grand-children and future generations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, our social compact continues to be one where: One, the Government creates conditions for economic growth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Access to affordable quality education, housing and healthcare services, regardless of our background, becomes opportunities to flourish.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Everyone can live with dignity and be self-reliant to do the best for themselves and their families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Two, families continue to be the core of our society and our first line of support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Strong families in turn support the building of resilient individuals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because they play a big part in caring and supporting one another through the ups and downs of life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Three, the community plays an active role in helping those with less because we believe in a caring society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together, they form the foundation of our social compact.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, we will face a very different social landscape over the next 50 years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: New challenges, different from what our forefathers faced.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We needed to invest considerable resources into enabling our seniors to age with grace, as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will be more challenging to finance, amid a shrinking labour force.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While our socio-economic strategies have uplifted broad segments of our population in the past, our current and future challenge would be to ensure that those at the bottom continue to progress upwards alongside the rest of the society on a moving escalator.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, many of these individuals and families face differing and complex needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The tried and tested solutions of the past need revisiting.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There will always be inequality in any society, in one form or another, sometimes even within a family.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we must keep opportunities alive for all Singaporeans to ensure social mobility.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It cannot only be for those who have the resources, but for everyone, regardless of where they start in life and where they are today.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must get this right, no matter how difficult.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because if we fail, Singapore will go down the path of becoming a fractured and disunited nation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In essence, we want everyone in Singapore to be happy because they succeed in our society of opportunities that the Government continues to create.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At MSF, we will help those faced with transitional difficulties to bounce back and enable those with disabilities to participate, contribute where they can, and benefit from our society of opportunities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need those who have succeeded to give back for the betterment of society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many have done well, not only through their own efforts, but from an enabling system that provided the opportunities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must also resist the natural tendencies for society to stratify, and actively encourage social mixing in our housing, National Service and public spaces that we all treasure together, like our hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF's work contributes to uniting our people, across social classes, backgrounds and groups through their generosity and kindness, to give back, creating a stronger sense of togetherness in our society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Enabling, uniting and caring – these are at the core of our mission in MSF.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration Desmond Lee, Minister of State Sun Xueling and Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will subsequently elaborate more on our other initiatives – and they all revolve around enabling, uniting and caring for each other.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, many Singaporeans, including Members of this house, have shared about their wishes for Singapore to be a more inclusive society, which provides opportunities for all.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: No one should feel that they will be at a disadvantage because of their life circumstances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will make our society more inclusive for Persons with Disabilities, or PwDs, including children with developmental needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During my earlier speech at MOH's Committee of Supply, I shared with members about the importance of the early years in building resilience.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With this, MOH launched the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being strategy – with a focus on medically sound pathways.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the child's gift to the world can only be realised with a rich environment in which he or she grows up in.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our pre-schools are an important enabler for this and within our broader strategy to support families with young children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want to give every child a good start.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Evidence from local research like GUSTO, and our own practice and experience, tells us that intervening properly as early as we can, will in a big way prevent disadvantages from snowballing later in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the early years, our KidSTART practitioners focus on equipping parents with relevant knowledge and skills on child development, parent-child interaction, health and nutrition.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When the child is older, about age three onwards, we focus our efforts on facilitating their enrolment into our quality preschool system.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These will also be progressively implemented alongside the scaling up of ComLink which Minister Desmond Lee will share more on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As strong and resilient families provide our children with a nurturing environment to row, we have put in place a continuum of family services to meet different needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also continue developing the Families for Life, FFL, movement to help all families build strong relationships upstream and foster a community-based ecosystem of support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling will elaborate further on these in her speech.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, during the Emerging Stronger Conversations, many Singaporeans shared with us about their desire for a more inclusive society for PwDs across life stages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam also asked if existing efforts to encourage inclusiveness have been successful and if more can be done.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have stepped up efforts to raise public awareness of disability issues and inclusion through campaigns, such as “See The True Me”, which reported more positive attitudes towards PwDs amongst viewers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the years, MSF has worked with the sector to enhance early intervention support for children with developmental needs through our network of pre-schools and early intervention centres.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Starting by instilling inclusive values and mindsets from as early on in life as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will lay the foundations for a more caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Studies show that both children with developmental needs and typically developing children can benefit from greater inclusion in pre-schools in areas like developing positive social attitudes and relationships, without compromising their development.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Building on existing efforts, we set up the Inclusive Preschool Workgroup to bring us closer to that vision.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They have come up with some recommendations to bring us closer to that vision, which Minister of State Sun Xueling will share more in her speech.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The second key area that we will focus on is helping individuals bounce back from the setbacks of COVID-19, in a manner that builds resilience.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When COVID-19 first hit, the Government mounted a decisive response.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We rolled out the Jobs Support Scheme to help businesses retain their workers and launched the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package to keep our workers economically engaged.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To cushion the impact on incomes, we rolled out various financial support schemes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While the situation in Singapore has stabilised, we recognise that the economic impact of COVID-19 will continue to be felt by many.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked for an update on the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) and how we are creating more jobs, especially in the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It provides temporary financial relief to lower to middle income workers impacted by COVID-19, as they look for new jobs or upskill to prepare for career changes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One example is Mr Lee whose employment contract ended last year and received support under CRG.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since his job loss, he attended three courses to upskill himself.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He shared that CRG helped to cover some of his living expenses, including transport expenses for job interviews and training sessions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He also recently secured a part-time job as a packer to supplement his CRG.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He is confident that his training will put him in good stead to transit to full-time work soon.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want to enable workers just like Mr Lee to bounce back from their setbacks and do well for themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This support is complemented by a national drive by the National Jobs Council to create new jobs to help those who are affected.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singaporeans can look forward to opportunities in the early childhood and social service sectors, as well as within the MSF family.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A key thrust is also the creation of opportunities for PwDs through the existing Open Door Programme and new initiatives including the Place-and-Train, Attach-and-Train, and Skills Development programmes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One example is Ms Kelly Ong, a graduate from APSN Delta Senior school who lost her job during the circuit breaker when her employer stopped operations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As part of SG Enable’s Job Placement Job Support Programme, a job coach helped Kelly with the job search process and prepared her for interviews.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Eventually, Kelly found a job as a kitchen crew at a restaurant given her interest in the F&B industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to support others like Kelly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together, these will put us in a good position to actively build resilience in our people and enable them to bounce back from the crisis even stronger.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In response to Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Seah Kian Peng, I will share more about how we are doing so in three areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Digital transformation, building organisational excellence and capability, and strengthening partnerships with the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Digitalisation is a core pillar of our transformation journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To this end, we are developing Industry Digital Plans for both the early childhood and social services sectors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They will provide structured frameworks to help preschools and Social Service Agencies (SSAs) optimise resources and business processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will improve efficiency, support professionals in their work and raise the quality of services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Next, we will strengthen support for SSAs to drive organisational excellence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We rolled out the Transformation Support Scheme to co-fund SSAs to hire manpower in areas of transformation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It will be made available next year to provide longer term support for SSAs’ capability- and capacity-building needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In response to Ms Carrie Tan, the CCT will build on existing capability building efforts and expand them so that SSAs have continued support to transform themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Xie Yao Quan also asked what MSF is doing to encourage more giving during these challenging times and to harness the power of the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF will continue to renew our social compact in a manner that builds a caring society with a strong sense of mutual help and giving back.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Corporates and individuals have been giving regularly to Community Chest’s SHARE.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Deputy Prime Minister had earlier announced, Change for Charity is a new initiative to empower giving through everyday consumption habits.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: From FY2021, Community Chest will work with businesses to enable customers to donate through their transactions on payment platforms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This can be conversion of loyalty points to donations or even direct donations at point of payment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will increase this dollar-for-dollar matching, if businesses also match customers' donations, adding up to three dollars in total.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I was very glad to hear Mr Seah Kian Peng putting up his hand for NTUC Enterprise to be the first to come onboard and hope many other companies will join us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Corporates can receive a one-off grant to support the implementation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During the Emerging Stronger Conservations, many Singaporeans expressed their desire to be more involved in efforts to care for those in need.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to strengthen our partnerships with the community, in the spirit of SG Together.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We agree with Mr Melvin Yong that care-givers play an important role in our social safety net.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During my earlier speech at MOH’s Committee of Supply, I spoke about strengthening support for care-givers of seniors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At MSF, we will embark on a similar effort to support care-givers of PwDs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS, SG Enable and community partners will form a Singapore Together Alliance for Action for care-givers of PwDs in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will complement the Third Enabling Masterplan, which I spoke about earlier.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Denise Phua also shared about a similar alliance for the Autism Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, if there is a partnership that we must build, it is between our men and women.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: All of us know women close to us – our mothers, our wives, our sisters, our daughters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They deserve our respect and to be celebrated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As a whole, we have done well in many areas – enabling our women to access quality education and healthcare services, and higher labour participation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have provided them with safe and secure neighbourhoods and streets, where women can be out late at night alone without worrying about safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A luxury that is uncommon in many other cities and communities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The recent spate of sexual offences and violence against women are abhorrent.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They somewhat reveal how some of our boys and men view women.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And my colleague Minister Shanmugam has made a Ministerial Statement to this end.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But our partnership with our fellow Singapore women cannot stop there.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also look into other areas that have been frequently brought up.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The on-going Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development aim to explore how we can do better collectively for Singapore women at home, in workplaces, in schools, and in the community on these various issues.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling will elaborate more in her speech.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In Malay):    COVID-19 has brought about many challenges to societies around the world, thus becoming one of the most pressing social crises of this modern age.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Those who have been facing challenges continue to be hit by problem after problem, as the Malay proverb goes "someone falls, and the ladder falls on him, too".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we will face a very different social landscape in the future, bringing with it various new challenges.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our socio-economic strategies have uplifted broad segments of our population.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
