text: However, the challenge is to ensure that those at the bottom can continue to progress alongside the rest of the society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must ensure that opportunities are kept available for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: No matter how difficult, we must ensure that social mobility remains achievable within the established social structure.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because if we fail, Singapore will go down the path of becoming a fractured and disunited nation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must also not forget those close to us – our mothers, sisters, wives and daughters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must ensure that women who need protection are protected, those less fortunate are given help, and those with career aspirations are given the opportunity to achieve it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They deserve our respect and are to be celebrated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to partner you, help the less fortunate and support the aspirations of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In English): In my previous Ministry, we did everything we can to save our planet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But leaving good children to take care of our planet is as important as leaving a good planet for our children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In Singapore, we have progressively strengthened our social compact over the years and took a pragmatic approach, as our society evolved and our resources enabled us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are now faced with an immediate problem to renew our social compact as we tackle the uncertainties of a future global economy scarred by the pandemic that can either deplete our resources or enable us even more.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The long-term impact of climate change will severely tax our resources, too.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our pioneers set the foundations of Singapore and painted our society with hope amid a crisis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the background of the uncertainties of separation, we saw hope in building a metropolis together.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similarly, we must ask ourselves: what kind of society do we want to be over the next 50 years?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What kind of society do we want to leave our future generations?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: How we each decide to act in the face of adversity will shape our values and norms for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For us at MSF, the crisis presents an opportunity to build more resilient individuals and stronger families, with a more caring and resilient society, characterised by greater inclusivity and opportunities for all.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We need everyone, and a whole-of-society approach and effort to bring us closer to that vision of home.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I look forward to our continued partnership with fellow Singaporeans and Members of this House to build a better future for ourselves and our children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together, I am confident that we can emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Chairman, Minister Masagos has just set out our social compact and laid out MSF’s key focus areas for the year ahead.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: COVID-19 has had a profound impact on societies all around the world.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But it has also brought out the best in Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the past year, many more Singaporeans stepped forward.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Government, community and corporates partnered one another to support our neighbours, our friends and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This foundational work served us well when COVID-19 struck, especially during the Circuit Breaker.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Others offer their premises as “Safe Sound Sleeping Places”, or S3Ps for short, and these provide localised interim shelter.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Officers from MSF and MND join the partners’ outreach walks to offer assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They work closely with PEERS members to support homeless rough sleepers with housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Early last year, there was an urgency to provide shelter to rough sleepers because of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For their safety, we needed to find rough sleepers safe shelter quickly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF called for more groups to open their premises as S3Ps.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And this was a six-fold increase from pre-COVID-19 times.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also worked with HDB to provide vacant flats as temporary S3Ps. d.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The eventual goal is to help them address their underlying social issues and achieve longer term stable accommodation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another example was the outreach effort to households living in rental flats, which commenced last June.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We wanted to ensure these households were coping well with the pandemic, as they were much more vulnerable, and to offer support where necessary.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We activated the SG Cares Community Networks to support this outreach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The local Networks were started in 2018 to bring together the social, health and community sectors in each town, to strengthen social, health and community integration.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These examples demonstrate clearly how important networks of trust are during a crisis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Denise Phua asked how we work with social service agencies and community partners to deliver social services in a coordinated manner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach has been to organise our support around each family’s needs and practise what we called the 3Cs earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And to achieve this, MSF has trained nearly 4,300 officers to assess underlying issues and to deliver more comprehensive support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Frontline officers can connect those in need to relevant support, if the families’ issues go beyond their own agency’s remit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This shift, which is a work-in-progress, emphasises a family-centric approach, instead of adopting an agency-centric lens.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will be training community partners and volunteers next, who are important touchpoints to render even more comprehensive support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Besides building capabilities, we have also integrated processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One example is the plan that Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim mentioned to strengthen information exchange between Singapore Prison Service and the FSCs – he described this during MHA COS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This enables offenders’ families to receive timely support from FSCs and community partners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another example is Streamlined Assessment Protocols, or SAPs, that allow ComCare clients to access other forms of help schemes more easily.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They now qualify for medical assistance at public healthcare institutions, childcare subsidies and MOE Financial Assistance without having to be repeatedly means-tested.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF is working with other agencies to set up new protocols, so that clients can seamlessly access assistance via other agencies, beyond the SSOs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Don Wee had suggested making the help-seeking process more seamless for low-income vulnerable families by sharing data across Ministries and integrating the application processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is, indeed, something we are working on with the relevant agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will make better use of data and technology to improve our clients’ experience and our officers’ productivity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, some clients have to repeat their circumstances and submit similar documents repeatedly to apply for different schemes from different departments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Officers often spend time collecting information that is already available with another agency.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This time can be better spent building trust and rapport.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The systems enhancements that we mentioned at last year's COS to improve data-sharing between agencies are coming on-stream this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One platform is what we called One Client View, or OneCV, which was rolled out last month to officers from 12 agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the past, the household who wanted to apply for rental housing, ComCare assistance and childcare subsidies, for example, had to submit income documents three times to these three different agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With One Client View, the family can do away with these submissions and simply give consent for agencies to retrieve the information through this platform.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One Cilent View has multiple levels of safeguards built in to ensure that such personal data is kept safe.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another platform, called Case Connect, will be rolled out in phases from June this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, collaboration takes place over different modes – emails, phone calls, messages, handwritten notes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Valuable information can get lost when case workers change, or new partners come onboard, and you can imagine many, many agencies are involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To reduce the administrative burden on frontline officers and our social service agency partners, we integrated the systems with single sign-in and will progressively build system linkages.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, not just focusing on our clients, but ensuring that our frontline, both in Government and in the social service sector, they find it meaningful, they find it seamless and they find it integrated for themselves, too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Case coordination can become challenging with more partners involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To drive integration, we will take a regional approach to organise key social services because, in reality, if you ask the different agencies, they tend to serve the same families, the same households in the same locality.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our aim is to have a common set of partners serve the same community in the same region.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This helps to reduce coordination costs and promote better integration across agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been organising many of our programmes with this regional approach in mind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include KidSTART and Community Link or ComLink, which Minister Masagos had shared about earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also set up regional Strengthening Families Programme @ FSC to support early-risk and stressed families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling will elaborate more later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These programmes will be organised along SSO regional clusters, so that agencies can easily work with the partners in the same region, build relationships among each other to convene case discussions and coordinate support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In turn, this strengthens the SG Cares Community Network in each town.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: During the Emerging Stronger Conversations that we have had, many Singaporeans expressed their desire to build a society that cares even more deeply for the vulnerable and less privileged.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng also asked how we will build stronger partnerships with the community to support those in need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will strive to achieve this through the SG Cares Community Networks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a Singapore Together Alliance for Action, or AfA, which focuses on prototyping new ideas to solve problems.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Networks also provide a platform where local partners in a town, with Government agencies, charities, social service agencies and other community groups get to know one another face to face, collaborate and, over time, build a relationship of trust in the local community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have seen the collective impact of the Networks earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we believe we are just starting to tap on its potential, and we call on more community partners and volunteers to join our efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Community Link, or ComLink for short, is a flagship initiative that seeks to pull together the elements that we talked about earlier: achieving deeper integration, putting families at the centre of our work, being proactive, building strong local networks, and partnering the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng and Minister Masagos had announced the expansion of ComLink earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, now, let me provide some details, which will also address Mr Mohd Fahmi's cut on ComLink's progress and future plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Carrie Tan asked if ComLink is taking an asset-based community development, or ABCD, approach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Yes, elements of ABCD are in ComLink but ComLink is more than that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under ComLink, instead of waiting for households to seek help, we proactively reached out to families with young children who are living in rental housing to understand their needs, their fears and their aspirations, listen to their voice.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We pulled together data across agencies and used them to identify issues faced by families as well as assets and gaps in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Community partners came together to coordinate support for families with complex interlocking issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We came up with common action plans and journeyed with the families to support them in achieving their goals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, data driven needs identified by our outreach to the families, hearing and listening to them, and tailoring those support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our objective is to systematically uplift families with children living in rental housing and support them towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Theresa is a single mother with two children and had difficulty holding down a stable job because of the difficulties she faced.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ever since the Social Service Office (SSO) knocked on her door two years ago as part of ComLink, Theresa gradually opened up to share her challenges and aspirations of becoming a childcare teacher and her hopes of owning her own HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Her social worker and community partners came together, provided her coordinated support and worked out with her a case plan, a progress plan, a roadmap.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, Theresa is a confident parent with stable employment who contributes back to her own local community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SSOs will continue to drive this effort with relevant Government agencies, social service agencies and community organisations through ComLink Alliances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we step up efforts to do more for vulnerable Singaporeans, we need to redesign the way we deliver services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a natural evolution of the social safety nets that Minister Masagos has set out in his opening frame.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And what is this new way of delivering social services?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Achieve social impact that many volunteers and donors yearn to see.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are testing out these ideas at selected ComLink communities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ComLink is an ambitious enterprise premised on the belief that Government, SSAs and the community come together at the national level, supported by resources and the right policies, we can make a much bigger impact in uplifting the low-income and vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Social sector practitioners have told us that what we are trying to achieve is critically needed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, we are doing this because of their sound advice and guidance over the years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They tell us this is much needed but not easy to achieve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We must confess that with no precedent to rely on, we are feeling the stones as we cross the river.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I am confident that we can cross the river to the other side because of our common desire to build a society that cares more deeply for those who have less.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to roll up our sleeves, make an impact and see the difference.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, Minister Masagos, Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling, Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua and I would like to invite Singaporeans to be a part of this movement on the ground.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those who are keen to join us can approach a Volunteer Centre set up by MCCY in your town or sign up through Volunteer.sg portal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleagues and I look forward to working with more of you to build a Singapore where no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Masagos shared MSF's plans to strengthen our social compact, including strong families as our first line of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is on these points that I would like to elaborate today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, our families are the foundation of society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must support them to the best of our ability, across their differing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, our women are key members of our families and society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will support them so they have real choices, so that they do not have to choose between family and their careers, and can achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will provide them with a good start in life so that they may grow up to be resilient members of our society and form strong families of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, to build strong, resilient families, we have in place a continuum of family services to support families with varying needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, for soon-to-wed and married couples, we support them in building strong foundations in marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will grow the Families for Life movement to strengthen family ties and bonds and we will promote evidence-based programmes for marriage preparation and parenting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Seah Kian Peng will be happy to know that we will help families who show early signs of stress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SFP@FSC will bring together programmes and support services for marriage and divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will start a family counselling service, including for families with early signs of stress, so we can mend relationship fissures early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some marriages need more support, such as those who marry before 21 years of age, or transnational couples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Tailored marriage preparation and support programmes will help lay a strong foundation for marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will step up support for families undergoing divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Services will be more accessible as families may approach any of the 10 SFP@FSCs whereas the DSSAs may not be located as conveniently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SFP@FSC will adopt an integrated, regional and multi-disciplinary approach to family service provision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Bringing early-risk family services under SFP@FSC allows better oversight of family services and greater integration of support for families with multiple needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SFP@FSC will be organised according to the 10 SSO regions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Upstream preventive measures for all families and downstream interventions for early-risk families and those with complex needs will be accessible in the same location.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To address multi-faceted and complex family issues, the SFP@FSC will bring together a multi-disciplinary team of professionals skilled in family counselling, financial counselling and psychology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We expect to scale up to five SFP@FSCs, with three more social service agencies working with MSF by the last quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The remaining five will be rolled out within the next two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On family violence, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked what can be done to create a community of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Minister of State Assoc Prof Mohammad Faishal and I co-chair the task force on family violence, which has studied the landscape and possible causes of family violence so that we can intervene effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have conducted focus group discussions and we are currently reviewing feedback from partners and Members of the House.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The task force is developing recommendations to break cycles of abuse and offending under four broad thrusts: (a) increasing awareness and strengthening societal attitudes against violence; (b) making it easier for victims and the community to report violence and to get immediate help; (c) strengthening protection for victims to reduce their risk of being harmed again; and (d) increasing the burden of accountability placed on perpetrators and strengthening their rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will next share how we will continue to support our women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our women's contributions are integral to the Singapore Story and we must celebrate and support their continued progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ahead of Monday, I would like to wish everyone, both men and women, Happy International Women's Day in advance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the profile of participants and issues raised at the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So far, we have conducted 37 conversations and engaged over 1,800 individuals, including youths, working mothers, homemakers and women leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Men make up almost a quarter of our participants, and I know that more will come.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Participants raised concerns ranging from challenges faced by working mothers to violence against women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During my Budget speech last week, I mentioned that participants from our Conversations on Singapore Women's Development raised concerns on the approach for punishment for hurt and sexual offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am heartened to hear the Minister for Home Affairs and Law present the Ministerial Statement on the review of the sentencing framework for sexual and hurt offences in Parliament today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is a strong step to further safeguard the protection and safety of our women and girls.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Participants at the conversations also raised the need for mindset shifts and suggested establishing support networks in workplaces and the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Increasing representation of women in corporate leadership was also raised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar that we need more women leaders for diversity in skillsets, experiences and perspectives, which leads to better decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Next, I would like to talk about how we ensure that every child has access to affordable and quality pre-schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairman, it is paramount that every child is provided with a good start.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For families with young children, we have stepped up efforts to enhance the accessibility, affordability and quality of pre-schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Subsidy amounts also increased across all eligible tiers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We enhanced the Partner Operator (POP) Scheme, from January 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the new term, we lowered fee caps for POP centres from $800 to $760 for full-day childcare per month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also increased the number of POP centres by 30%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Low- and middle-income families can additionally receive up to $28,000 in means-tested subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Louis Chua asked about accessibility and quality of pre-school places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an important point that affects young families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many Members of Parliament have raised this issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Back in 2019, together with my colleagues Cheng Li Hui, Rahayu Mahzam and Cheryl Chan, we pushed for more accessible and affordable quality pre-school places, especially in new towns with many young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government promised in 2019 that 80% of pre-schoolers would have a place in Government-supported pre-schools by around 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have significantly increased the number of full-day preschool places, from about 120,000 in 2015 to around 190,000 today – an increase of over 50%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are thus on track to grow the total number of full-day pre-school places to 200,000 by 2023 and achieve the Government’s promise by around 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have increased the number of early childhood educators from 18,000 in 2018 to over 22,000 last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We support the professional development of our educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One such effort is enhancing the capabilities of educators teaching Mother Tongue Languages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA partnered the National Institute of Early Childhood Development, or NIEC, in 2019 to introduce Certificate courses for Malay and Tamil language teaching.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A course for Chinese language teaching will be introduced later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how we will support lower income families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2021, we plan to expand KidSTART, to Choa Chu Kang, Bukit Panjang, and Bukit Batok, on top of the regions already announced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the Growing Together with KidSTART initiative, we forged new corporate partnerships with SP Group and The LEGO Group, and deepened existing partnerships with Prudential Singapore and Etonhouse Community Fund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will tap on individual and corporate volunteers to build stronger, long-lasting relationships with KidSTART families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about childcare services for shift workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Childcare centres can operate beyond standard operating hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, over 40 childcare centres operate beyond 7 pm on weekdays.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Others may arrange for care-givers such as relatives to help out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of the Community Link pilot, we sought feedback from some 650 families and community partners, including on care-giving arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are studying the possibility of piloting night-time childcare at a ComLink site.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children with developmental needs, it is paramount to identify needs early and provide the necessary support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our children are precious and we must create environments where they can thrive, and they can feel included and accepted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We, therefore, set up the Inclusive Pre-school Workgroup, or IPWG, which Minister Masagos spoke about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through the IPWG, which I co-chair, the Government has worked with partners across the health, education and social sectors to study how we can better support children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about efforts to strengthen inclusion in pre-schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The workgroup will release its report in April.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ahead of this, let me broadly share the upcoming initiatives.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The workgroup has a tiered support framework, depending on the level of early intervention support required.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The introduction of ICOs will set a baseline for the sector’s support for children with developmental needs and signal that every pre-school has a role to play in strengthening inclusion.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICOs will work with early childhood educators to flag children with potential developmental needs for further assessment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will connect teachers and parents to early intervention support or resources, such as our Development Support-Learning Support programme (DS-LS).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA will work with pre-schools to support appointed staff with appropriate training.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICOs alone are not the silver bullet and we urge all pre-school leaders and educators to partner ICOs in their pre-schools in this inclusion journey.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In Tier 2, we will expand the DS-LS programme and the Development Support Plus (DS-Plus) programme to more pre-schools, to support children requiring low levels of early intervention support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under the InSP, pre-schools will be resourced with full-time early intervention professionals who will work with early childhood educators.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will reduce the logistical strain faced by care-givers, of shuttling between pre-schools and early intervention centres, and provide more integrated support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The IPWG recognises there are children who require higher levels of early intervention support and who remain best served in a separate specialised early intervention setting.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA will follow up on IPWG’s recommendation to study integration opportunities for these children in Tier 4.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA will also strengthen the capabilities of the early childhood and early intervention professionals in our efforts to make pre-schools more inclusive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ultimately, strengthening inclusion in our pre-schools will benefit both children with developmental needs, and typically developing children, with enhanced teacher training, and development of stronger social skills from a young age.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: (In Mandarin):    Families are the foundation of our society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Hence, we have in place a continuum of family services to support families with varying needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In 2019, we piloted two Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centres (SFP@FSC) with two Family Service Centres, which will bring together programmes and support services for marriage and divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In support of women, the Government and community organisations have organised 37 conversations as part of the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development, engaging more than 1,800 people from various backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: During the conversations, participants raised various concerns, such as challenges faced by working mothers and violence against women.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to gather feedback and study the suggestions put forward by the participants and submit a White Paper to Parliament in the second half of the year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the area of pre-school education, we are stepping up our efforts to provide more accessible, affordable and quality pre-schools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will increase the number of Government-supported pre-school places, to meet the target set in 2019, of 80% of pre-schoolers having a place in Government-supported pre-schools by around 2025.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, we will work towards every pre-school appointing an Inclusion Coordinator to provide early intervention support for children with developmental needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will also expand the Development Support- Learning Support Programme and pilot a new Inclusive Support Programme to help children who travel daily between pre-school and Early Intervention Programme for Infants & Children centres.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will also further support low-income families with young children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will expand KidSTART this year to benefit low-income families living in Choa Chu Kang, Bukit Panjang and Bukit Batok.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: An important part of the programme is to ensure that young children are adequately nourished.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under KidSTART, practitioners will work directly with parents to guide them on their children's nutritional needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our community and corporate partners will also come in to support families with food sponsorships where necessary.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Regardless of their family background and difficulties they face, we want to create an inclusive and warm school environment for them, so that every child can thrive, overcome the challenges in their lives and education, and develop to their full potential.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This requires the concerted effort of all of us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This begins from nurturing our youth to bring out the best in them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All youths, including our vulnerable and at-risk ones, can be resilient individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We must support them well, so they too can realise their full potential.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked how we can do so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through the Localised Community Network (LCN) pilot, we provide wraparound, coordinated support to children and youth with complex family circumstances or those who exhibit at-risk behaviours.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF also works closely with appointed agencies to run programmes aimed at reducing at-risk behaviours, such as "Youth GO!".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over the years, we have made steady progress.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Pre-court diversionary programmes have significantly contributed to keeping first-time youth offenders who commit minor offences out of the court system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to work with our partners to build a preventive support system for our youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will pilot a mentoring programme targeted at students who leave ITE prematurely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have two main objectives: First, to expand the youths’ network of positive relationships.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope that the young mentees will find lifelong friends and role models in the mentors, pick up useful life skills, and gain access to a trusted adult that they feel comfortable reaching out to.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, to empower the youths to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope to broaden their exposure to opportunities and support them in building on their strengths and talents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We intend to gather mentors from various industries, to guide the youths to explore potential careers in areas they are interested in.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond this, we invest upstream in family and community resources to address risks and disadvantages as early as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we also regularly review our legislation to better safeguard the welfare of our youth and children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the impact of the amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) passed by Parliament in 2019.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Most amendments took effect from July last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We extended protection to older children who are abused or neglected, by raising the age limit from 16 to 18.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The shift from “Beyond Parental Control” to “Family Guidance Orders” emphasises the family’s responsibility in guiding their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Now, parents and children must attend a family programme, before parents can apply to the Court for a Family Guidance Order.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The intent really is to equip families with ways to resolve conflict and strengthen family relationships to avoid the need for the Court to intervene.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The regime is still new at this point in time, and we need time to monitor its implementation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are also enhancing our capacity and capability to rehabilitate youth offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It would take resources, time to strengthen safety and security, before MSF Youth Homes are able to take in additional youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And on a related note, we are also reviewing the Adoption of Children Act (ACA); to seek public feedback on proposals to better safeguard the welfare of adopted children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our efforts would not be possible without close collaboration with the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Minister Masagos mentioned, we are strengthening partnerships with the community, and encouraging the spirit of giving and volunteering to uplift our vulnerable communities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman asked how we are empowering our youths to contribute to building a resilient and inclusive society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many youths have been leading and igniting change through community initiatives, and we are actively partnering them to channel their energy and ideas for good.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I will be sharing more examples later on in my speech.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mental well-being is a pertinent issue of our time, brought to the fore by the pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the start of the circuit breaker, MSF and MOH set up a dedicated National Care Hotline, to provide psychological first aid to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The hotline has since managed over 40,000 calls since it commenced operations in April last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And in the recent months, with the gradual lifting of COVID-19 measures, total calls managed has decreased and stabilised to 1,500 calls a month, including about 450 per month that needs emotional support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But beyond this, there is more that we must do as a society to promote mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked how the Youth Mental Well-Being Network (YMWBN) will help support youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Network gives us a platform to brainstorm with the community and try out new ideas to better support our youths’ mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Minister of State Xueling shared at MOE’s Committee of Supply, Network members have initiated over 30 potential projects to date.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I took part in a brainstorming session in October last year, and was very heartened and inspired by the many good ideas exchanged.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One such initiative is Driving Resilience & Inspiration for The Incredible Next Generation, or DRIFTING in short.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Led by Network members Ms Francesca Wah, Mr Caleb Tan, Mr Jerry Seah, Mr Pang Lim and Mr Chan Ming Hui, DRIFTING is an outreach programme that aims to provide positive peer support for at-risk adolescents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Tapping on the experiences of former youths-at-risk and informal community touchpoints such as hairdressers, mama shop owners, DRIFTING seeks to strengthen the social support network and introduce protective factors for at-risk adolescents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The team will soon be ready to recruit volunteers and conduct outreach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our youths are also actively involved in causes to help the vulnerable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Seventeen-year-old Brendson Tan has been involved in ground-up initiative Mummy Yummy since 2013, when his grandmother started the initiative with three other mothers to distribute meals to families in rental flats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As deputy lead of the youth team, Brendson leads over 200 youth volunteers to distribute food door-to-door.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And he also leads weekly house visits in Bedok to check on residents’ well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Increasingly, youths also want to have a voice in the policy-making process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We constantly find ways to involve youths in our consultations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, the Youth Advisory Group (YAG) provides their perspectives to the NCPR, which I co-chair with Minister of State Faishal.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In recent years, MSF, community agencies, and religious organisations have also joined hands to form various networks to address social issues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I recently joined the Catholic Welfare Services and the Homeless Hearts of Singapore on their night walks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On one walk, we met two uncles who shared their concerns about safety and about losing their belongings when they sleep rough.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They were actually initially quite hesitant to move into a shelter, but upon our MSF officers follow up especially on the very next day, they went to engage the uncles again, giving them assurance that the shelter would be suitable and adequate for their needs; they eventually moved into the shelter.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And they are now in touch with HDB and MSF SSOs to gradually work out their housing and financial needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope that more Singaporeans will join us in stepping forward to make a difference.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):    Every youth has the potential to become an adaptable and resilient individual.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In recent years, we also collaborated with community agencies and religious organisations to set up many platforms to study and address various social issues, such as youth mental well-being, rough sleeping, vulnerable groups in the community, charity food support and so on.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to work with Singaporeans to build a society centred on resilience, care and inclusivity so that we can continue to thrive in the face of future challenges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In English): In closing, let me round back to the questions that Minister Masagos posed earlier: What is our shared vision for the future?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: What kind of society do we want to be, and what legacy do we want to leave for our future generations?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From conversations with the public to spirited discourse with members of this House, we share a vision to build a society where all Singaporeans have access to opportunities to achieve their dreams and that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF will continue to work with all Singaporeans to build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring and inclusive society, so that Singapore can thrive no matter what the future brings.

text: It is Friday and it is almost half past eight.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But to all the men and women in this space, the social service space, we know that they work very quietly, but very hard behind the scenes throughout the years.
